title: Chandrasekhar limit: how massive a white dwarf can be
summary: On his voyage from India to Cambridge in 1930, Chandrasekhar calculated the maximum mass of a white dwarf star.
why: Key to understanding neutron stars and black holes.

unsung.contribution: Calculated the mass limit above which a dead star cannot become a stable white dwarf.
unsung.recognition: Arthur Eddington openly criticised the theory in 1935 and refused to accept it; the Nobel Prize came only in 1983.
